Running away score before the incident.
Free text attached to the Flashscore incident, when present (about 78% of rows).

Flashscore live-commentary lines from -1 to +3 minutes around the incident that carry the VAR icon, VAR or video wording or the word 'disallow', joined with ' || '. Mostly written as commentary, not an official log.

True if any such commentary line exists or the incident text mentions the video assistant referee. Looser than 'explicit VAR wording': it also fires on a generic 'disallow' line (1 Getafe incident in the 394).

Derived class: offside by goalscorer, offside by teammate in build-up, offside player not identified, foul, handball, other.
What the goal would have meant given the score before it: Go-ahead / opener, Extend lead, Equaliser, Reduce deficit.
Final goals scored by `team` in the match (actual result).
Points if `team` had scored one more goal and nothing else changed (fixed-score what-if).
pts_if_allowed minus pts_actual for this incident alone.
True if the fixed-score what-if changes the match result (points_lost > 0).

True if an ESPN review-type event (overturned goal, VAR no-goal decision, or any 'Video Review' / VAR decision line, including 'decision on field stands/cancelled') lies within 3 minutes; blank if no ESPN match record. It does not by itself show that a goal was overturned.
Offside flags against `team` (an officiating outcome; see threats to validity).
